name: AURA
tagline: Your crew's health, even when Earth is 20 minutes away.
description: Astronaut health monitoring for long missions far from Earth. AURA compares every reading with the astronaut's own preflight baseline, gives a Normal, Warning or Critical status with the reason, forecasts trends 14 days ahead, and says what to do next. Transparent rules set every level; Claude AI explains and coaches, with an offline fallback for every AI feature.

event.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
event.challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions

features: Personal preflight baselines and an adaptive in-flight baseline
Normal / Warning / Critical alerts from transparent, cited rules
Daily countermeasure plan, symptom triage and plausibility checks
Radiation dose budget against NASA-STD-3001 limits
Message ground with the real signal delay and delivery status
Flight surgeon console: a person plays the ground live from a second device
Ground view with printable reports and a crew wellbeing score
Gamified routine: streaks, badges, weekly challenges, crew board
Ask AURA: typed or spoken questions (on-device Whisper), spoken answers, auto-navigation, memory
Real NASA OSDR Inspiration4 bloodwork, cytokines and protein panels with an AI review
CSV import of your own data and custom indicators
Dark and light themes, phone layout, WCAG 2 AA audited

nasa_data.use: Inspiration4 metabolic panel, immune cytokines, cardiovascular proteins, serum 200-plex

synthetic_data: The demo crew's telemetry is synthetic (seeded simulator) and labelled as such.
disclaimer: Hackathon prototype. Thresholds are research-informed prototype rules, not clinically validated flight-medicine limits.
